SMTO-EXE-0023 — SMTO couldn't show or update Fast Cache

GUID: 0fc1209a-08cd-484a-a2ba-c6236e8f2590
Slug: cache-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • Something went wrong inside SMTO while it was showing or changing your saved Fast Cache procedures, so your change may not have gone through. Normal tasks still run as usual.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Fast Cache and select Refresh. This shows whether your pin or removal went through before you try it again.
  2. If your change isn't there, make it once more. This problem can be brief, and one new try is safe once you've seen the change didn't apply.

What success looks like

  • The Fast Cache list loads and shows your pinned or removed entry as you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting whether you were pinning, removing or just opening Fast Cache. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or saved files to clear this; they hold your conversations and saved procedures.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Fast Cache management request (list, inspect, pin or remove) failed with an unexpected exception and was returned as a fixed 503 cache_unavailable; the response does not establish the cause.

What this means

  • Execution-cache management caught an unexpected service exception outside the specific ineligibility path. The generic response does not establish storage failure as the cause. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Execution-cache management caught an unexpected service exception outside the specific ineligibility path. The generic response does not establish storage failure as the cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the cache endpoint and bounded service diagnostics; distinguish a management failure from an execution failure or eligibility rejection.

How to fix it

  • The route replaces the exception with a fixed detail, so reproduce the same /api/agent/fast-cache request and inspect FastCacheManagement for the failed prerequisite (for example access to the current-run database at agent_current_run_db_path), then restore it. Do not delete cache or receipt data or weaken eligibility checks to clear it; re-list Fast Cache afterwards to confirm the intended change.
  • Inspect the cache-management failure and restore its actual failed prerequisite; ordinary execution remains subject to its existing checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The requested cache management action succeeds and its list/state reflects the intended change.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
